narration.text: A laid-off analyst's three clocks are kept: unemployment filed this week, COBRA for October only to cover a scan, a marketplace plan and credit from November, and severance signed to be paid after thirty days, while a withdrawn draft, an early payment, a full COBRA, a December start and a broker's rush are left out, across four portals. This is a chore for a 52-year-old logistics analyst in New York, laid off with six weeks of severance and a scan on the sixth of October, who has a broker's rush, a friend's advice and a COBRA notice. On the bench, she found 6 of 6 eligible items, worth 6,025 dollars of the 6,025 dollars there was to find. She made no false claim. The world held 8 traps, and she walked past 8. She took 2 minutes. By hand, the same chore takes 3 hours, so she was about 78 times faster. The verdict: exceeds. She beat the bar this playbook set itself. The bar was 75 percent of the money, no false claim and inside 60 minutes. Every card she filed waited for a person's signature, and nothing was sent.
